# Quadratic Variation of $X(s) = W_{s+\epsilon} - W_s$

## Setting Up the Problem

I need to compute $[X]_t = \lim_{n\to\infty} \sum_{i=1}^n (\Delta X_i)^2$ where $\Delta X_i = X(t_i) - X(t_{i-1})$ for a partition $\Pi_n: 0 = t_0 < t_1 < \cdots < t_n = t$ with mesh $|\Pi_n| \to 0$.

**Key observation:** Define $Y(s) = W_{s+\epsilon}$ and $Z(s) = W_s$, so $X = Y - Z$. Both $Y$ and $Z$ are Wiener processes as functions of $s$, giving $[Y]_t = t$ and $[Z]_t = t$.

By the bilinearity of quadratic covariation:
$$[X]_t = [Y-Z]_t = [Y]_t + [Z]_t - 2[Y,Z]_t$$

## Computing the Cross-Variation $[Y,Z]_t$

With a uniform partition $\Delta t_i = \delta = t/n$, the increments are:
$$\Delta Y_i = W_{t_i+\epsilon} - W_{t_{i-1}+\epsilon} \quad \text{(over } [(i-1)\delta+\epsilon,\; i\delta+\epsilon])$$
$$\Delta Z_i = W_{t_i} - W_{t_{i-1}} \quad \text{(over } [(i-1)\delta,\; i\delta])$$

**For $n$ large enough** (i.e., $\delta < \epsilon$), we have $(i-1)\delta + \epsilon > i\delta$, so the two intervals are **disjoint**. Therefore:

$$\Delta Y_i \perp\!\!\!\perp \Delta Z_i, \qquad \mathbb{E}[\Delta Y_i] = \mathbb{E}[\Delta Z_i] = 0, \qquad \text{Var}(\Delta Y_i) = \text{Var}(\Delta Z_i) = \delta$$

## Showing $[Y,Z]_t = 0$

The cross-variation is $\lim_{n\to\infty}\sum_i \Delta Y_i \Delta Z_i$. Since the increments are independent:

$$\mathbb{E}\!\left[\sum_i \Delta Y_i \Delta Z_i\right] = 0$$

For the variance, using that $\Delta Y_i \Delta Z_i$ are essentially independent (cross-covariances vanish when $\delta \ll \epsilon$):

$$\text{Var}\!\left(\sum_{i=1}^n \Delta Y_i \Delta Z_i\right) = \sum_{i=1}^n \text{Var}(\Delta Y_i \Delta Z_i) = n \cdot \delta^2 = t\delta \;\xrightarrow{n\to\infty}\; 0$$

By the Chebyshev/Borel-Cantelli argument, $\sum_i \Delta Y_i \Delta Z_i \xrightarrow{\text{a.s.}} 0$, so:
$$[Y,Z]_t = 0 \quad \text{a.s.}$$

## Final Computation

Substituting into the decomposition:

$$[X]_t = [Y]_t + [Z]_t - 2[Y,Z]_t = t + t - 2(0) = 2t$$

**Intuition:** $X(s)$ is the difference of two Brownian processes whose increments are asymptotically independent (the time lag $\epsilon$ ensures non-overlapping increments as the partition refines). The quadratic variation adds for independent components, giving $2t$.

$$\boxed{2t}$$
